questions.question: A run ends with stop_reason max_steps. What does that tell you?
options: Only that it didn't finish in time; you need the trace to learn why
That the model is too small
questions.explanation: The step budget is a safety net. Diagnosis needs the pattern inside the trace.

questions.question: The trace shows calculator('round(1.06)') -> error, calculator('1.06') -> 1.06, then the same pair again. Which pattern is it?
questions.explanation: Two calls alternating A, B, A, B. Not an error streak, because every other call succeeds.

questions.question: Why does the watchdog nudge first instead of forcing an answer immediately?
options: A specific nudge often fixes the run with a real, tool-grounded answer; forcing gives up on tools
Nudges are cheaper than tool calls
questions.explanation: In the demo, a model that listens fixed its call after one nudge. Forcing is the fallback for models that don't.

questions.question: Why convert ReAct text transcripts into native tool-call form before diagnosing?
options: One internal shape lets every detector stay simple, while still reading the traces you actually have
questions.explanation: Adapters at the edge, one shape inside. A doctor that can't read your trace format is useless.

questions.question: In this lesson's live runs, how did llama3.2 usually fail with native tool calling?
options: It gave up early: tool calls written as text, or answering itself after one call
questions.explanation: 9 runs, no loops: 4 text tool calls and 5 early answers. Detectors must cover premature stops as well as loops.

questions.question: Many runs get stuck because the calculator has no rounding. What's the most structural fix?
options: Change the tool contract: add rounding, or make the error say rounding isn't supported and show what is
questions.explanation: Fix the cause (the tool's contract) before adding loop machinery around it.
